gaps.term: each transform layer is a contraction
gaps.note: The page defines a contraction as a linear map that does not increase the largest coefficient magnitude, then asserts that every transform layer is one, without showing why a layer built from sums of complex roots-of-unity multiples keeps that maximum from growing.

The page says only that truncation rounds a coefficient to a multiple of 2^{-p}. It does not say the rounding is to the nearest multiple or how the real and imaginary parts are bounded, so the reader cannot check the per-truncation bound.

gaps.term: total error stays below 1/2 for suitable p
gaps.quote: Choosing $p$ large enough as a function of $n$ keeps the total below $1/2$, since there are only as many truncations as transform rounds.
gaps.note: The page does not say how many transform rounds there are as a function of n, nor how the per-truncation errors add up to a total bound. The reader cannot check that a precision p exists that keeps the total below 1/2.
